newsitem.title: USA: McDonald's adding three deluxe sandwiches.
newsitem.headline: McDonald's adding three deluxe sandwiches.

text.p: McDonald's Corp plans a national roll-out of three deluxe sandwiches next week -- two chicken and one fish -- which analysts said will help the chain bolster its menu in an intensely competitive U.S. market.
McDonald's has not officially announced the sandwiches, which were tested in Cincinnati, Ohio, and Fresno, California.
But asked if they were being launched nationally, McDonald's spokesman Chuck Ebeling said Thursday, "I guess it's fair to say that."
The new sandwiches, along with the four-month-old Arch Deluxe hamburger, are being launched as the U.S. restaurant industry ends a summer of soft sales, analysts said.
Thus McDonald's strategy is to freshen up its menu in hopes of drawing in more customers.

"I think it's a step in the right direction," Merrill Lynch analyst Peter Oakes said of the new sandwiches. "Either McDonald's gets more business from existing customers or they bring in new customers. I think this can do a little bit of both."

The new sandwiches include grilled chicken breast, breaded and fried chicken breast and a fish fillet, with lettuce and tomato. McDonald's is expected to launch the new menu offerings with a media event on September 26.

McDonald's new sandwiches, like the Arch Deluxe, are expected to be aimed primarily at the adult market. But it remains to be seen if the sandwiches, along with the Arch Deluxe, will draw in and keep new customers, analysts said.
McDonald's said earlier this month that the Arch Deluxe added incrementally to sales in the second quarter and continued to do so in the third.
"We're of the view that the roll-out of the original Arch Deluxe was pretty much a non-event," Schroder Wertheim analyst Wayne Daniels said. "It's clear it did not help customer traffic."
Dean Witter analyst David Adelman, however, said he believes the Arch Deluxe was successful in terms of attracting attention for McDonald's.
"I see no reason to think it (Arch Deluxe) is not successful," Adelman said. "For any product to fundamentally change a business, that is an inappropriate expectation."
Adelman added that he believes Arch Deluxe and the new sandwiches are part of McDonald's evolution to a menu that emphasizes product innovation instead of a price-based menu.
"They are trying to de-emphasize price and emphasize product attributes," Adelman said.
